text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a sharp latency + throughput drop for a Private VPC customer in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-14 10:15 UTC. Symptoms: P95 spikes, tail latencies, and overall RPS falling off. Initial hypothesis: NAT egress saturation combined with a KV-cache miss storm after we flipped the kernel selector earlier today. link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/vpc-egress

maria: Which customer and which runtime version? Any immediate logs?

alex: Customer: acme-media (private). Runtime: private-runtime v1.9.2 -> we rolled kernel selector to prefer optimized AVX kernels at 09:58. Repro/profile snippets below (top of profile at peak):

alex: ```
# perf top-ish aggregate (sampled stacks)
50.2%  runtime_dispatch::select_kernel
22.6%  epoll_wait
12.8%  sendto
8.5%   kv_cache::lookup (miss path)
6.0%   tcp_sendmsg
```

sam: epoll_wait + sendto heavy — could be egress/NAT queueing. Did conntrack or iptables counters spike? Also check MTU/DF drops.

alex: Checked conntrack:
```
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count -> 64192
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max -> 65536
ss -s shows many TIME-WAIT/estab sockets
```
We also see a huge increase in ephemeral SNAT allocations in cloud provider NAT metrics (allocation failures + retries).

maria: What about KV cache metrics? If kernel change changed syscall/blocking behavior it could increase small-request rate and bypass cache priming.

alex: KV cache hit-rate timeline: 2026-03-14T09:45: 98% -> 10:15: 61% (concurrent cold starts up). Per-request tokens up ~3x.

jordan: Two-prong: 1) NAT/conntrack exhaustion + MTU/reassembly issues could make TCP a lot slower. 2) Kernel selector change might have altered batching heuristics (we saw earlier that AVX path reduced micro-batching window). That pushed many small requests through, increasing request-per-second and SNAT churn.

sam: Quick mitigations we can run now: 
- bump nf_conntrack_max to 200k (sysctl)
- pin the private runtime nodes to use dedicated NAT GW (remove shared NAT path)
- temporarily rollback kernel-selector change for the private runtime Canary
- increase batch_timeout to 30ms and reduce batch_size target to 8 for the affected route

maria: Can we also check MTU mismatch? Last time a partner router had 9000 MTU while host was 1500 and we saw reassembly stalls. Run `ip link show` and check `dmesg` for PMTU blackhole.

alex: Ran ip link on a node — MTU=1500 across the fleet. No PMTU dmesg entries. The cloud NAT logs show heavy SNAT retry/backpressure. I force-applied conntrack bump + pinned egress to dedicated NAT GW for the customer's subnet at 10:36. Also rolled back kernel selector for the private fleet Canary at 10:42 and applied batching tweak to the route.

perf-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0283; perf regression PERF-432 created and linked.

alex: Early effect: by 10:55 P95 latency dropped from 320ms -> 95ms, throughput recovered ~85% of baseline. KV cache hit-rate climbing back toward 90% as we feed the warmed prefixes. NAT conntrack utilization dropped to ~40%.

jordan: Follow-ups (action items):
- add an e2e perf test that simulates high-small-request workloads in Private/VPC with shared NAT to catch conntrack/NAT saturation in CI.
- add alerting: `kv_cache_hit_rate < 75%` and `nat_conntrack_utilization > 70%` (both for private VPC customers).
- include kernel-selector perf smoke in release gating for private runtime changes.

maria: Also add a docs note for on-call runbook: if private customer has persistent small-request burst traffic, consider per-subnet dedicated NAT GW and batching overrides.

sam: One more: consider per-pod SNAT or pod-level egress throttles + conntrack accounting so noisy neighbors can't exhaust the host.

alex: Agreed. I'll file follow-ups and tag infra/security for NAT quota changes and customer ops for a maintenance window to keep dedicated NAT long-term. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
